title: An accounting firm cannot prove how AI touched client work that may later be challenged
job: Capture productivity gains while preserving evidence, review and accountability for client work.
trigger: Professional uses AI on engagement material.
surfaceComplaint: We know people use AI, but we do not have a defensible engagement record of how.
believedCause: We need a stricter AI policy.
mechanism: Adoption has moved faster than controlled workflow integration. Unauthorized tools can create missing provenance: what data was sent, what AI produced, and who checked it.

economics.painCostNote: Thomson Reuters reports 35% of tax/audit firm professionals use unauthorized AI.

buyer.roiLogic: Protects client trust and evidence while enabling AI.

distribution.acquisition: Start with approved tools and one engagement workflow.

experiment.success: 100% of sampled pilot uses reconstructable to input/output/reviewer with no material slowdown
experiment.kill: existing vendor already provides full provenance or users bypass flow

claims.text: Thomson Reuters reports 35% of tax and audit firm professionals use AI tools their firm has not authorized.
The same report says 81% regularly use AI in day-to-day workflows.
Missing AI provenance in an engagement record is a productizable liability gap.
